---
name: etxtbsy-fake-binary-flake
description: "Text file busy" in strategy hook tests is an ETXTBSY fork race on a test-written fake binary, not a hook bug; the visible assertion is a red herring
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`TestGitHookCommitMsg_MissingEntireStillRunsChainedHook` (and any sibling that
writes a fake executable and execs it through `sh`) flakes on Linux CI with:

```
--- FAIL: TestGitHookCommitMsg_MissingEntireStillRunsChainedHook
    hooks_test.go:1481: backup hook did not run: stat .../COMMIT_EDITMSG.backup-ran: no such file
        /tmp/.../commit-msg: 6: dirname: Text file busy
```

**The assertion is a red herror — read the captured subprocess output.** "backup
hook did not run" is downstream of `dirname: Text file busy` (ETXTBSY): the hook
died at line 6 before reaching the backup.

Mechanism: golang/go#22315. `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks_test.go:1458` writes a
fake `dirname` into a temp dir that `envWithPath` (:1507) makes the *entire*
PATH. Between `os.WriteFile`'s open-for-write and its close, another parallel
test in the same binary forks (`hooks_test.go` alone has ~33 `t.Parallel()`, and
the package shells out to git constantly) and the child inherits the write fd.
Exec of that file then returns ETXTBSY until the child closes it. Go's `os/exec`
retries ETXTBSY for commands *it* starts — this exec is inside the `sh`
subprocess, so nothing retries.

Fix if it recurs: symlink the real `dirname` (`exec.LookPath` before overriding
PATH) instead of writing a script — the fake reproduces `${1%/*}` exactly, so a
symlink is behaviour-identical and is never an ETXTBSY target. Same exposure at
`:1425` (`fakeEntire`), `:751`, `:823`, `:844`, `:1249`, `:1289`; those need real
scripts, so they'd need a write-then-verify-exec helper instead.

Unrelated to whatever PR it appears on: `git diff main...HEAD -- hooks_test.go`
was empty when this hit CLI #2038; the fixture came from `d672f4987`.

name: ci-race-in-login-tty
description: "How to read the CI failure where ~30 unrelated cli tests fail at once — it's one -race report, not a panic"
metadata:

Diagnosed 2026-08-14, fixed in PR #2006.

**Symptom that misleads:** `test` / `test-core` fail with ~30 unrelated failures in
`cmd/entire/cli` at once (`TestMergeUnique`, `TestActivityModel_ScrollKeys`,
`TestBuildRepoDir`, …). That breadth is not systemic breakage and usually not your
change — one failure kills the test binary and Go reports every test in the package
as failed.

**It was a data race, not a panic.** `grep "panic:"` over `gh run view --log-failed`
finds nothing, because the real marker is `WARNING: DATA RACE`. Only the `-race`
jobs (`test`, `test-core`) catch it; `test-integration`, canary, and Windows all
pass, which is itself a hint. Grep for `DATA RACE` and read the two stacks.

**The bug:** `readLoginURLActionFromTTY` (`login.go`) closed its TTY with an
unconditional `defer`. Bubble Tea's `shutdown(kill bool)` only joins the input
reader when `!kill`, and context cancellation takes `shutdown(true)` — so
`ultraviolet.TerminalReader.StreamEvents` can still run after `Run()` returns. On
Linux that reader is `cancelreader`'s epoll implementation, whose wait loop reads
`tty.Fd()`, racing `poll.(*FD).destroy()`. macOS uses a different cancelreader that
never touches `Fd()`, so it **never reproduces locally** — CI on Linux is the only
verification.

**`Program.Wait()` is a trap here.** It looks like the way to join the reader but
waits on `p.finished`, which `Run()` closes via its own `defer` — so it returns
immediately, and on the one early return where `p.finished` is still nil it would
block forever. There is no API to await that goroutine; the fix is to not reclaim
the descriptor on the cancelled path.

**How to apply:** when a Go package reports many unrelated test failures in CI but
passes locally, (1) grep the log for `DATA RACE` before `panic`, (2) check whether
only the `-race` jobs failed, and (3) suspect platform-specific code paths before
suspecting your own diff — and don't call it a flake on one green run. See
[[hook-benchmark-methodology]] for the related trap of trusting a single sample.
==========

Under `-race` on **darwin**, a Go test that forks could die with `signal: segmentation fault` in
the child before `exec`. **Go toolchain bug, FIXED IN go1.26.5** (released 2026-07-01).

**Root cause.** Go 1.26 turned darwin's `syscall.rawSyscall` from a bodiless
runtime/assembly declaration into a real Go function (`rawsyscalln` refactor) without adding
`//go:norace`. `syscall.forkAndExecInChild` is `//go:norace` and justified calling rawSyscall
because "they are assembly functions" — true on darwin until 1.26. So under `-race` the fork
child ran TSan instrumentation and faulted in `__tsan::TraceSwitchPartImpl` (null ThreadState
field deref, SIGSEGV at `0x8`). Upstream: golang/go#79804, CL 786620, 1.26 backport #79806.

**The fix, verifiable locally:**
`diff ~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.{4,5}/src/syscall/syscall_darwin.go`
→ 1.26.5 adds `//go:norace` to `rawSyscall`, `rawSyscall6`, `rawSyscall9`, `errno`, `errnoX`,
`errnoPtr`, and corrects the `exec_libc2.go` comment. **So: bump the Go pin (mise.toml +
go.mod) rather than disabling `-race`.** Affected range is go1.26.0–1.26.4 only.

CLAUDE.md was updated to match ("records never live on the shadow branch"). Both PRs are up, CI in flight.

## Shipped

**[#2094](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2094) — Factory E2E onto the task-record contract.** Replaced the shadow-branch poll with two helpers that pin the new contract in both directions:

- `waitForCompletedTaskRecord` — polls `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` for a record with a non-empty `completed_at`. `omitempty` drops the zero value, so presence *is* completion. Same strength as the existence check it replaces.
- `assertNoShadowTaskData` — the inverse, and the same assertion #2032 added to its own integration test. Narrowed to `/tasks/` paths rather than "no shadow branches", because a parent session legitimately has shadow branches of its own (pinning keys on `StepCount`).

Renamed to `TestFactoryTaskRecordExistsBeforeCommit` — no pre-commit *checkpoint* exists under the new model, but the durability intent in the name is still what's tested. Also fixed `factoryai_worker_session_test.go`'s header comments, which named the renamed test and still described the pre-#2032 model.

**[#2095](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2095) — ETXTBSY.** Symlinks the real `dirname` instead of writing a stand-in, so there's no written-then-exec'd file for a forking sibling to hold a write fd on. Verified with `-race -count=20 -parallel 16`.

Both: `mise run fmt && lint` clean, `test:ci` green (canary 56/56 and 4/4).

## Two things I want to flag rather than bury

**#2094 does not answer the durability question, and its green build shouldn't be read as if it did.** Before #2032 a Worker's transcript was on the shadow branch the moment the turn ended; now it's a state record with a declared path into the agent's own file, materialized at condensation. If that's a real weakening, #2094 makes the tests agree with the weaker behaviour. It's stated plainly in the PR body and left with #2058. If you'd rather I chase it, that's the follow-up I'd pick next.

**#2095 deliberately leaves six sibling sites un-hardened** — `fakeEntire` and five others have the same write-then-exec shape but need to be real scripts, so they'd need a write-then-verify-exec helper. None has been observed flaking. Scoped and visible in the PR rather than fixed speculatively; say the word if you want the whole class closed.

The remaining gap neither PR touches: `E2E Tests` runs on push-to-main only, which is *why* #2032 couldn't be caught in review. The Worker task path has no pre-merge coverage, and the canary is free and deterministic — that's the structural fix, and it's a separate change.
